pr.body:
We're adding one more step in the GitHub integration installation pipeline, namely GitHub OAuth2 authorize. This is transparent from the UX perspective as the data exchange happens without user interaction.

The pipeline will now fail in these cases:
- If there is a mismatch between currently authenticated GitHub user (derived from OAuth2 authorize step) and the user who installed the GitHub app (https://github.com/apps/sentry-io)
- If there is a mismatch between `state` parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature
- If GitHub could not generate correct `access_token` from the `code` (wrong or attempt of re-use of `code`).

In all those cases, this error is shown:
![image](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/assets/1127549/18923861-2ead-4cf5-adda-7738aef801d7)
pr.title: fix(security): validate GitHub user during integration installation

raw_findings.body: A KeyError is raised instead of the intended graceful error page, causing an unhandled 500 response during a security-sensitive validation step instead of the expected 'Invalid installation request' message.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Uncaught KeyError propagates as an unhandled exception instead of returning the intended error response.
raw_findings.impact: A KeyError is raised instead of the intended graceful error page, causing an unhandled 500 response during a security-sensitive validation step instead of the expected 'Invalid installation request' message.
raw_findings.root_cause: New equality check assumes integration.metadata always contains a 'sender' key with a 'login' subkey, but this is not guaranteed for all Integration records.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login") and treat a missing/empty value as a mismatch that triggers the error() response.
raw_findings.title: Unguarded access to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] can raise KeyError
raw_findings.trigger: A user re-installs a GitHub app whose Integration record already exists (no attached OrganizationIntegration) but was created before the 'sender' metadata field was populated (as anticipated by the existing guard `if "sender" not in integration.metadata` in src/sentry/integrations/github/installation.py), or metadata otherwise lacks the 'sender' key.

raw_findings.body: Because _() is now called on a variable rather than a string literal, Django's makemessages/xgettext static extraction will not pick up these strings, so they will never be added to .po translation catalogs and will remain untranslated in all non-English locales.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Translation extraction silently omits these strings, causing incorrect/stale localization for future translators.
raw_findings.impact: Because _() is now called on a variable rather than a string literal, Django's makemessages/xgettext static extraction will not pick up these strings, so they will never be added to .po translation catalogs and will remain untranslated in all non-English locales.
raw_findings.root_cause: Refactor replaced literal calls to _("...") with a generic error() helper that calls _() on a variable, which gettext tooling cannot statically extract.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the literal strings with _() at each call site (or pass already-lazy-translated strings) instead of deferring translation to a variable inside error(), e.g. pass error_short=_("GitHub installation pending deletion.") from callers and use it directly in error().
raw_findings.title: Error messages passed as variables to gettext break translation string extraction
raw_findings.trigger: Any call to error() with a custom error_short (e.g. error_short="GitHub installation pending deletion." or error_short="Github installed on another Sentry organization.") relies on _() translating that string at runtime.

raw_findings.body: The test now only validates the generic state-mismatch error path and no longer verifies the original behavior of surfacing 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' when the GitHub API returns 404, leaving that code path (and the responses.replace 404 stub) effectively untested/dead.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test passes but silently stops covering the originally intended installation-not-found scenario, masking regressions in that code path.
raw_findings.impact: The test now only validates the generic state-mismatch error path and no longer verifies the original behavior of surfacing 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' when the GitHub API returns 404, leaving that code path (and the responses.replace 404 stub) effectively untested/dead.
raw_findings.root_cause: Test update introduced an incorrect state value that causes an earlier, unrelated validation branch to trigger instead of the intended 404-handling branch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the correct pipeline signature/state value in this test so the flow reaches the installation-lookup 404 branch, and re-add an assertion on the specific installation-not-found error message.
raw_findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 installation-not-found code path
raw_findings.trigger: The test supplies a mismatched 'state' value ("ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05") instead of the pipeline signature used elsewhere ("9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"), which causes OAuthLoginView to short-circuit on the state-mismatch check before ever reaching GitHubInstallation.build_integration/get_installation_info that would hit the mocked 404 response.

raw_findings.body: Real, unexpected failures (unrelated to normal 'missing access_token' cases) are silently converted into a generic 'Invalid installation request' error with no logging, hiding root causes and complicating debugging/observability of installation failures.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unexpected errors are masked as generic user-facing failures, reducing observability and making production issues harder to diagnose.
raw_findings.impact: Real, unexpected failures (unrelated to normal 'missing access_token' cases) are silently converted into a generic 'Invalid installation request' error with no logging, hiding root causes and complicating debugging/observability of installation failures.
raw_findings.root_cause: Overly broad exception handling introduced around the token-exchange response parsing without logging.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the except clause to the specific expected exceptions (e.g. UnicodeDecodeError) and log unexpected exceptions before returning the generic error response.
raw_findings.title: Bare except silently swallows errors during GitHub OAuth token exchange parsing
raw_findings.trigger: Any exception during reading/decoding/parsing the OAuth token response (e.g. network error, malformed body, encoding failure) is caught unconditionally.

finding.title: Bare except silently swallows errors during GitHub OAuth token exchange parsing
finding.trigger: Any exception during reading/decoding/parsing the OAuth token response (e.g. network error, malformed body, encoding failure) is caught unconditionally.
finding.verifier_reason: While the bare except at lines 425-429 does catch all exceptions, the code immediately checks for access_token and returns error() if missing. This is intentional fallback behavior for OAuth token exchange failures. The claim of 'no logging' is accurate but this is a design choice for user-facing errors, not a bug. Impact is observability concern, not functional defect.
